gap: No result ChatGPT got states Apple's own rules for the iPhone itself: 'if the battery gets too warm, software might limit charging above 80 percent', and while a USB-C or Lightning accessory is connected, wireless charging is capped at 10 W on iPhone 17 Pro/Pro Max, 7.5 W on every iPhone 16 model and 16 W on iPhone 17, iPhone Air and iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max. Apple also says iPhone 16 and 16 Pro peak at 22.5 W, not 25 W.
standout_why: I compared four of the results ChatGPT got. Macworld's car-charger roundup (cited) only says the iPhone Air is 'limited to 20W'. It has no 80% cap, no limit when an accessory is plugged in, and no 22.5 W cap for iPhone 16/16 Pro. MobilePlusTech (cited once) says only 'When an iPhone gets hot it slows charging', and that 25 W applies to iPhone 16 and 17. That is wrong for the 16 and 16 Pro under Apple's own figures. MobileReviews Eh! (cited) gives bench numbers but no reason why the phone limits charging. ESR's product page could not be loaded (rate-limited). I did not open Macworld's 'best MagSafe chargers' article. Our own current page also leaves out all three Apple rules.
decides: The phone, not the mount, sets the charging speed, so the pick depends on the shopper's iPhone and car setup. First, any USB-C accessory plugged into the iPhone caps wireless charging at 7.5 to 16 W. In that case a 25 W cooled mount gains nothing over a cooled 15 W mount like the ESR HaloLock CryoBoost. Whether a wired CarPlay cable counts as such an accessory is not documented by Apple. Second, iPhone 16 and 16 Pro top out at 22.5 W, and iPhone Air at 20 W. Third, the cooling's real job is to keep the battery out of the 'too warm' state, where iOS stops at 80% or pauses charging. In MobileReviews Eh!'s bench test, the ESR OmniLock put 19.1 W into the battery with a 35.3 °C peak surface temperature. Anker's thermoelectric (TEC) A2933 drew 21.9 W but put only 11.7 W into the battery, and it needs a 45 W+ input. That supports the ESR OmniLock for 25 W-capable iPhones. It counts against the Anker and against any thermoelectric mount run on a weak car port.

findings.label: iOS limits charging above 80% when the battery is warm
findings.value: "To extend the lifespan of your battery, if the battery gets too warm, software might limit charging above 80 percent."
findings.source_title: How to use your MagSafe Charger with iPhone - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple's own wording. The charger cannot override it. The iPhone decides, so the job of active cooling is to keep the battery out of this state.

findings.label: Wireless charging cap while a USB-C/Lightning accessory is connected
findings.value: 16 W on iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max; 10 W on iPhone 17 Pro/Pro Max; 7.5 W on iPhone 16/16 Plus/16 Pro/16 Pro Max; 16 W on iPhone 17 and iPhone Air
findings.source_title: How to use your MagSafe Charger with iPhone - Apple Support
findings.note: Verbatim: "While you have USB-C or Lightning accessories such as headphones connected to your phone, charging is limited to ... to comply with regulatory standards." Apple's example is headphones. Apple does not say whether a wired CarPlay cable counts.

findings.label: Peak MagSafe/Qi2.2 wireless power by iPhone model
findings.value: 25 W: iPhone 18 Pro/Pro Max, 17 Pro/Pro Max, 17, 16 Plus, 16 Pro Max (30 W+ / 15V 2A adapter). 22.5 W: iPhone 16 and 16 Pro. 20 W: iPhone Air. 15 W: iPhone 17e and iPhone 15 and earlier
findings.source_title: How to use your MagSafe Charger with iPhone - Apple Support
findings.note: These are Apple's figures for its own MagSafe Charger. Anker's A2933 overview agrees in substance: 'iPhone 16 and Pro support up to 22W'.

findings.label: Heat pause, and car USB ports
findings.value: "Your iPhone might put charging on hold temporarily" ... "Charging will resume when the battery's temperature returns to its normal operating range." Also: "Charge ports in USB hubs or cars might charge slower than a dedicated USB-C charger."
findings.source_title: About iPhone charge speeds - Apple Support
findings.note: Apple's wording. It explains why the mount needs its own high-wattage USB-C PD adapter rather than the car's built-in port.

findings.product: Anker Prime Wireless Car Charger AirCool (A2933)
findings.label: Input needed for 25 W plus TEC cooling; iOS requirement; price
findings.value: 45 W+ input (15V⎓3A); 60 W dual-port car adapter included; iPhone 16 or later on iOS 26 or later; $89.99
findings.source_title: Anker Prime Qi2 25W Wireless Car Charger (MagGo, Air Cool, Pad) - Anker US
findings.note: Anker's note: 'Use a 45W or higher USB-C adapter for 25W charging and proper cooling.' The page contradicts itself on iPhone 16 and 16 Pro: the overview says 22W, the FAQ says 'iPhone 16 and later up to 25W after software update (except iPhone 16e)'. Warranty terms are not stated.

findings.product: Anker Prime Wireless Car Charger AirCool (A2933)
findings.label: Measured power into the battery vs. power drawn
findings.value: 11.7 W average into the battery; 21.9 W drawn; 38.5% efficiency; 37.4 °C peak surface
findings.source_title: Top 3 Qi2 25W Car Chargers for iPhone 18 Pro/Duo (Tested & Ranked) – MobileReviews Eh!
findings.note: MobileReviews Eh! method: bare iPhone 17 Pro, 30 minutes from about 15%, Apple 140 W USB-C charger, bench test (not in a car), ambient temperature and iOS version not stated. The gap between draw and delivery is consistent with the TEC cooler using part of the input, but the reviewer gives no explanation.

findings.label: Measured power into the battery and temperature
findings.value: 19.1 W average into the battery; 25.8 W drawn; 74.5% efficiency; 35.3 °C peak surface
findings.source_title: Top 3 Qi2 25W Car Chargers for iPhone 18 Pro/Duo (Tested & Ranked) – MobileReviews Eh!
findings.note: Same MobileReviews Eh! method as above. This was the best of 11 mounts. LISEN 2E7179 came close: 19.0 W, 36.2 °C, 71.7%.

findings.label: Fan behaviour, adapter, and ESR's own explanation of slowdowns
findings.value: Fan under 25 dB, turns on automatically while charging and off when the phone is full or removed; 58 W adapter included; ESR: 'High temperatures can slow charging speed and limit power output'; ESR says a stop at 80% may be 'related to an iOS upgrade'
findings.source_title: ESR OmniLock Magnetic Car Charger (25W, CryoBoost, Air Vent) | ESR Help Center
findings.note: This is ESR's UK help center. ESR also tells buyers to use a case thinner than 2 mm and to keep metal and cards out from between the phone and the charger.
